aboutTitle: I read the way some people pray.
heroEyebrow: A personal reading & writing space by Nida
aboutBody:
I started keeping a reading log years before I called myself a writer, mostly because I kept forgetting how books ended. The log turned into margin notes, the margin notes turned into essays nobody asked for, and eventually I ran out of room in my own notebooks. Bookhearth is where the overflow lives.

This isn't a place built for hot takes or hauls. It's built for the specific, quiet pleasure of a sentence that's doing more work than it looks like — the kind you read twice, once for the meaning and once for the craft. I write book reviews the way I'd talk about a book with a friend who hasn't read it yet: honestly, a little biased, and always with spoilers clearly marked.

The stories and flash fiction here are mine too — first drafts of a longer career, published slightly braver than feels comfortable.

What Bookhearth is for

It's for the reader who finishes a book and immediately wants to talk about it with someone. It's for the writer who needs proof that everyone's first draft is a little embarrassing. And it's for anyone who has ever rearranged a bookshelf by color, then by author, then by how much they loved each spine — you'll fit right in.

A short, honest bio

I've read in libraries, waiting rooms, and at least one wedding I probably should have been paying more attention to. I write in the mornings, edit in the evenings, and keep a stack of currently reading books that is, by any reasonable measure, out of control. Bookhearth is where all of it gets put to use.
heroLede: Bookhearth is a quiet corner of the internet for people who read slowly and always want to know what happens next.
